5. Specific commitments, goals and targets set by the entity with defined timelines, if any.

The material performance indicators have been determined from the materiality assessment carried out for TIL. Further, for each of material performance indicators, the goals & target metrices that have been derived are presented below, which we intend to achieve by the end of Indian FY 23/24: 1. Compliance with emerging ESG norms and expectation (Principle 1 and Principle 6) - We have created a compliance monitoring dashboard, which would eventually capture ESG norms, followed by formulating & implementing appropriate monitoring framework. By FY 2023-24,we strive to create entity’s sustainability and climate risk framework incorporating emerging global & domestic norms such as CBAM, CSDDD, CSRD etc. We will integrate ISO 37001 into our governance structure. 2. Manufacturing Process Efficiency and Transition to Low Carbon Ecosystem (Principle 2 and Principle 6) - We envision to enhance manufacturing process efficiency by conducting energy audits across the facilities and implementing appropriate procedures by FY 23-24, to reduce energy intensity of the products manufactured and switch over to low carbon intensive material and processes. 3. Environmental, Health & Safety (EHS) (Principle 3) - Reinforcing the existing EHS performance & risk management framework through periodic training interventions. We strive to incorporate six-dimensional hazard identification approach by FY 2023-24 inclusive BBS and establish infrastructure of ETP and work towards water neutrality. 4. Sustainable and Responsible Supply chain management (Principle 1, Principle 3, Principle 5, Principle 6) - We strive to develop & implement supplier and CSMS code of conduct for further executing suppliers Environmental, Social, & Governance - Due Diligence (ESG DD). 5. Climate related physical risk (Principle 6) - We will conduct scenario analysis to identify physical and transition risk associated with our business operations and implement strategies for its mitigation. 6. Logistics safety (Principle 1, Principle 3, Principle 5, Principle 6) - To ensure safe logistic movement we will conduct risk assessment and develop monitoring & evaluation framework. 7. Plant & Machinery: Utilization & health (Principle 1, Principle 6) - RCM based maintenance involved and continued through FY 23-24 8. Digitally integrating process and technology (Principle 4) - We shall conduct technical know-how analysis of the existing workforce to identify the gaps & accordingly deploy appropriate training module for skill upgradation, followed by conducting periodic assessment of the same. 9. Data breach prevention and management (Principle 9) - We shall strive to strengthen our data & and cyber security framework by implementing ISO 27001, inclusive of GDPR & NIST CSF. 10. Creating a culture of care (Principle 1, Principle 3 & Principle 5) - We strive to strengthen our human rights & governance requirements and align the same with UNGC principles, ILO guidelines and other domestic & international guidelines, such as ISO 37000 and ISO 26000 by the end of FY 23/24.

7. Statement by director responsible for the business responsibility report, highlighting ESG related challenges, targets and achievements (listed entity has flexibility regarding the placement of this disclosure)

We at TIL firmly believes in co-existence of mankind and nature for a sustainable future. We firmly believe to operate as a responsible corporate citizen and integrate sustainability in all aspects of decision-making procedures; and accordingly consider our impacts on the environment and society at large. At TIL we have initiated our journey of transition and placing efforts in value creation for better sustainability performance. Our stakeholders are of high importance to our business operations, and we endeavour to enhance their confidence in our business. Thus, to understand and capture the concerns of the stakeholders we have formulated a stakeholder engagement committee and taken appropriate measures to identify our key stakeholder groups comprising of internal & external stakeholders, followed by identification of material KPI’s through Double materiality assessment framework and appropriate stakeholder engagement and consultation process. Simultaneously, we have established strategies to mitigate the concerns identified by the stakeholders. To combat climate change and align with domestic and international goals on climate change at TIL, we have initiated certain measures to transit to a low carbon future. One of such steps was introduction of renewable energy to reduce our indirect carbon emission footprint, through the initiative of solar fencing. We appreciate the fact that use of fossil fuel in our operations is one of the major sources of direct emission, hence, we have been implemented processes to transit to cleaner fuels and have accordingly, adopted low carbon-intensive methods such as dual fired boiler, fuel switch to achieve higher energy output inclusive of reduced emissions. Post pandemic, the world as we know have changed; and as a responsible corporate citizen, we have initiated multiple efforts to uplift the society & local communities though our CSR initiatives. We endeavour to create a sustainable future where humanity thrives in correlation to nature.

73.24 In alignment with the TIL’s commitment to responsible operations and sustainable growth, several targeted capital investments were undertaken & proposed during FY 2024–25 to enhance both environmental integrity and social well-being across operational sites. The details of these strategic investments are as follows: Establishment of Chemlock and Explosives Storage Yard in compliance with PESO (Petroleum and Explosives Safety Organisation) regulations, ensuring heightened workplace safety and legal adherence. Upgradation of Siemens SCADA and PLC Hardware in the Banbury system to enhance automation, energy monitoring, and process control, thereby reducing emissions and improving operational transparency. Replacement of Ambulance (Over 10 Years of Service Life) to ensure timely and reliable medical response, reinforcing the company’s emphasis on employee health and occupational safety. Replacement of Bright Bars with Rails for the movement of all EOT cranes within the factory premises, contributing to enhanced structural safety, reduced wear and tear, and improved energy efficiency. Installation of Enhanced Drinking Water Facilities to improve employee welfare and hygiene, supporting the organization’s social sustainability objectives. Conversion of Boiler Fuel System to Dual-Fuel Capability, facilitating operational flexibility and a reduction in dependency on high-emission fuels, thus aligning with long-term decarbonization goals.
